question: Why does the 300 °C–300 °C multilayer urea crystal contain more nitrogen than the 300 °C single-layer crystal in the EDX results?
expect: premise false: it contains less nitrogen, 32.83 wt% against 35.15 wt% (more C and O), read as more cyanuric acid (Tables 9, 11; sec. 4.4)
rendered: The 300 °C–300 °C multilayer urea crystal does not contain more nitrogen than the 300 °C single-layer crystal. In fact, the EDX results show the opposite: the 300 °C–300 °C multilayer sample exhibits a lower nitrogen content (32.83 wt %) compared with the 300 °C single-layer reference (35.15 wt %).
